notes:
- Summary: Harborline is a large healthcare analytics vendor evaluating Redwood Private for PHI workloads (clinical summarization, Q&A over patient docs, embeddings for search).
- Deployment preference: Private VPC with customer-managed KMS; primary cloud GCP (us-central1) but open to AWS if HSM import available. They asked about support for external HSM and Cloud KMS/imported key material.
- Vendor intake: Received CAIQ v2025 + Harborline vendor risk spreadsheet. They need row-level answers (not just links to SOC2). Key focus areas: key custody and BYOK, audit log immutability and chain-of-custody, encryption in-transit and at-rest details, data deletion proof on offboarding, annual pen-test report, and HIPAA BAAs.
- SIG/CAIQ specifics: 25 items flagged as high-priority by Harborline security: K2 (KMS separation), A6 (network isolation/VPC peering), R1 (retention & deletion), I4 (access review + SSO integration), L3 (log export and retention controls). SE action: produce precise answers and architecture diagrams; include sample encryption envelope flow and rotation runbook.
- Shared responsibility: Harborline legal wants a signed appendix that explicitly maps Redwood responsibilities (runtime, managed kernels, OS patches, control-plane availability) versus customer responsibilities (data classification, KMS keys, in-VPC firewall rules, endpoint hardening). Also want an SLA for time-to-delete on offboarding (proposed 30 days) and verification steps.
- KMS/BYOK: SE notes: runtime can use envelope encryption with customer KMS; for GCP KMS we support CMEK integration + ability to reference external HSM via Import/Wrap workflows. Need ops runbook for key rotation and impact on KV cache. Harborline worried about key rotation causing cache invalidation and cold-start latency spikes. Action: provide mitigation plan (graceful rewrap + cache pre-warming).
- Audit logging: Customer requires immutable export to their SIEM (Splunk/Chronicle) and write-once storage. Proposal: forward logs via secure syslog over PrivateLink to their collector; provide S3/GCS export with retention controls. Need formal statement on immutability and attestable retention chains.
- Networking: Harborline requires no public egress for inference payloads; control plane traffic must traverse PrivateLink or VPC peering. They also require IP allowlist and private DNS. SE to supply network flow diagrams and NAT config examples.
- Compliance artifacts: Harborline requested SOC2 type II report, ISO27001 cert, HIPAA BAA template, and recent pen-test summary. They also want proof of annual appsec scan cadence.
- Commercials: Harborline prefers 3-year reserved Dedicated pool with a Private control plane add-on. ARR estimate 200k-650k depending on retention and BYOK integration SLAs.
- Customer quote: "We can move to procurement once we have granular SIG answers and a signed shared-responsibility addendum. BYOK is non-negotiable."
- Internal next steps: finalize CAIQ answers (SE Nikhil) by 2026-03-18; Legal to draft shared-responsibility appendix and BAA; Infra to prepare network diagram and KMS rotation/runbook.
- Risks: BYOK timeline, potential need for air-gapped option for certain PHI workflows, longer legal cycle for BAA.
notes_summary: Large healthcare customer evaluating Redwood Private (GCP-first) for PHI. Critical: CAIQ-level answers, BYOK (CMEK/HSM), immutable audit exports, signed shared-responsibility appendix and BAA. Procurement gated on SIG/CAIQ completion and legal sign-offs.
